subject: ClearWave order form — SLA exceptions rollup and maintenance calendar
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@clearwave.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clearwave.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Draft order form + MSA — high level SLA asks

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our internal draft of the Order Form and a redline against your MSA. High-level items we want to confirm before looping our procurement/legal:

- Uptime target: ClearWave needs 99.95% for the production tenant (we noted 99.9 in the MSA; please confirm).
- Service credits: we propose credits that begin at 15 minutes of downtime and scale quickly (we attached our table).
- Maintenance: we require a fixed monthly maintenance calendar with blackout exceptions for our peak dates (Oct–Dec), and we want confirmation that scheduled maintenance will be communicated 14 days in advance.
- P1 response / resolution times: we need a 30-minute response SLA and a 4-hour mitigation objective.

Can you review and let me know which of these Redwood can accept as-is, and which you want to counter? I attached the PDFs for reference.

Thanks,
Susan Lee
Director, Procurement — ClearWave
Attachment: ClearWave_draft_orderform_v2.pdf
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft order form + MSA — high level SLA asks

Kim / Marcus — forwarding ClearWave's draft. Key asks summarized above. My read:

- 99.95%: that's higher than our standard 99.9 for this tier but not impossible; it will materially affect credits and capacity planning.
- Credits starting at 15 mins: aggressive — we usually start at 30–60 minutes.
- Maintenance calendar + 14-day notice: reasonable, but we need a carveout for emergency security patches.
- P1 response 30m / mitigation 4h: ops can do a 30m page acknowledgement; 4h mitigation depends on root cause / cross-region failovers.

I drafted a proposed SLA exhibit (attached) that tries to meet them halfway: 99.95 with a capped credit ladder, credits kick in at 30 minutes, scheduled maint windows limited to two 4-hour windows per month by default (we can add seasonal blackout handling), and an emergency patch carveout. Please review redlines in the doc and add any legal language you want me to surface to their counsel.

Goal: get to a single-sheet of redlines we can send to ClearWave legal this week.

- Olga
Attachment: proposed_sla_exhibit.docx
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2027 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft order form + MSA — high level SLA asks

Thanks, Olga — reviewed the draft exhibit. My comments:

1) Uptime math: if we accept 99.95 we need to tighten the credit cap to protect business economics. Suggest credit ladder that maxes at one month of fees for sustained outages rather than multiple months.

2) Credits threshold: move to 30 minutes as a compromise (their 15m is too aggressive operationally). We can add an accelerated credit tier for >3 hours.

3) Maintenance windows: propose default "two monthly 4-hour windows" plus a mechanism to request additional windows for planned work. For seasonal peak blackout (Oct–Dec), add an approval flow where ClearWave can designate up to 6 blackout days per season with 60-day advance notice. Emergency security patches remain excluded (with a promise to notify within 4 hours).

4) P1 response: we can commit to 30-minute acknowledgement and an initial mitigation plan in 4 hours. Full resolution SLA should be "best effort"; don't commit to 4-hour full resolution unless on a per-incident scoping call.

5) Legal language: add a sentence limiting credits to fees paid within the 12-month period preceding the credit window. Also require that credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for service-level failures (standard).

If you want, I'll draft a short cover email to ClearWave legal that frames these as commercial compromises to keep the uptime target.

- Kim
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@clearwave.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clearwave.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form + MSA — high level SLA asks

Olga, Kim — appreciate the fast turn. A few counterpoints from our side after internal review (legal attached a redline):

- Uptime: we can consider a credit-capped 99.95 but need the credit start at 15 minutes for P1s. If you must move it to 30 minutes, we want the max credit to reflect a commensurate risk (we proposed up to two months of fees).

- Maintenance blackout: the seasonal blackout proposal with 60-day request is workable, but we cannot have unscheduled maintenance that affects production during our designated blackout dates. Emergency security patches are acceptable but only with prior notice when possible; we can't agree to a 4-hour notice for every emergency patch — some will require faster action.

- Response/resolution: 30-minute acknowledgement is OK. For mitigation, we need a clearer definition for "mitigation plan" and a commitment to an escalation path that includes a named on-call contact during the first 4 hours.

Attached is our redline (pdf). We're flexible on the credit cap if you can provide stronger operational guarantees: runbook access, dedicated incident contact, and a scheduled monthly operational review.

Next steps: can you send a single redline document combining our asks and Redwood's counter? If we can see a single document, legal will be able to sign off faster.

Thanks,
Susan Lee
Attachment: ClearWave_requested_changes.pdf
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@clearwave.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 17 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form + MSA — high level SLA asks

Susan — thanks for the clear counter. We've consolidated and accepted most commercial points with the following final positions (see attached final redline):

- Uptime: Redwood will accept 99.95% for the production tenant.
- Credits: credits will begin at 30 minutes (compromise) with an accelerated ladder that increases after 3 hours; we capped maximum credited amount at one month of recurring fees.
- Maintenance calendar: we agree to two 4-hour monthly maintenance windows by default and will honor up to 6 seasonal blackout days with 60 days' notice from ClearWave. Emergency security patches remain an exclusion; Redwood will notify you within 4 hours and will avoid customer-impacting work when an alternative exists.
- P1 response: 30-minute acknowledgement; mitigation plan within 4 hours; Redwood will provide a named primary on-call contact for the first 4 hours and a monthly ops review cadence.

Next steps: I've attached a single redline (redwood_final_redlines_orderform_20270417.pdf). If that looks good to ClearWave legal, I can issue the DocuSign envelope for the Order Form and Exhibit A. If they want additional tweaks to credit caps, please ask them to mark the pdf and return.

Proposed cover email (short):
"Please find attached Redwood's consolidated redline reflecting commercial compromises to reach 99.95% uptime. For any remaining legal language tweaks, please mark the single doc and return; our counsel will process redlines via the attached DocuSign link to expedite signature."

Please confirm and we'll circulate the envelope.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_final_redlines_orderform_20270417.pdf
